{{short description|American chemical engineer (born 1957)}}
'''Douglas S. Clark''' (born 22 May 1957) is an American chemical engineer.

== Education and career ==
Clark earned a bachelor's degree in chemistry from the [[University of Vermont]] in 1979,<ref name="cornelladvcouncil"/><ref name="ucbresearch"/> and graduated with a doctorate in chemical engineering from [[Caltech]] in 1983,<ref name="cornelladvcouncil"/><ref name="ucbchem"/> where he was advised by [[Jay Bailey|James Edward Bailey]].<ref name="aichesbeaward2014"/> Clark joined the [[University of California, Berkeley]] faculty in 1986,<ref name="cornelladvcouncil">{{cite news |title=Douglas S. Clark |url=https://www.cheme.cornell.edu/cbe/about/advisory-council/douglas-s-clark |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220420194501/https://www.cheme.cornell.edu/cbe/about/advisory-council/douglas-s-clark |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 20, 2022 |access-date=9 October 2023 |publisher=Cornell University Smith School of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering}}</ref> where he later held the Gilbert Newton Lewis Professorship, and has served as editor in chief of the scientific journal ''[[Biotechnology and Bioengineering]]'' since 1996.<ref name="ucbchem">{{cite news |title=Douglas S. Clark |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/faculty/cbe/clark |access-date=9 October 2023 |publisher=University of California, Berkeley College of Chemistry}}</ref><ref name="ucbresearch">{{cite news |title=Douglas Clark |url=https://vcresearch.berkeley.edu/faculty/douglas-clark |access-date=9 October 2023 |publisher=University of California, Berkeley Research}}</ref> In 2013, Clark was named dean of the [[UC Berkeley College of Chemistry]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Douglas Clark tapped to be next College of Chemistry Dean |url=https://biosciences.lbl.gov/2013/05/09/douglas-clark-tapped-to-be-next-college-of-chemistry-dean/ |access-date=9 October 2023 |publisher=Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory |date=9 May 2013}}</ref> He is also affiliated with the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], as a chemical faculty engineer.<ref>{{cite news |title=Douglas S. Clark |url=https://biosciences.lbl.gov/profiles/douglas-s-clark/ |access-date=9 October 2023 |publisher=Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory}}</ref> 

In 1995, Clark was elected a fellow of the [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]].<ref>{{cite news |title=DOUGLAS CLARK, PH.D. |url=https://aimbe.org/college-of-fellows/COF-0178/ |access-date=9 October 2023 |publisher=American Institute of Medical and Biological Engineering}}</ref> The [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] granted him an equivalent honor in 2003.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sirica |first1=Coimbra |title=AAAS members elected as fellows |journal=Science |date=31 October 2003 |volume=302 |issue=5646 |url=https://go.gale.com/ps/i.do?id=GALE%7CA110621586&sid=googleScholar&v=2.1&it=r&linkaccess=abs&issn=00368075&p=HRCA&sw=w&userGroupName=anon%7E8fdf3d73&aty=open-web-entry}}</ref> In 2014, Clark received the [[Jay Bailey|James E. Bailey]] Award for Biological Engineering from the Society for Biological Engineering, affiliated with the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]].<ref name="aichesbeaward2014">{{cite news |title=Douglas Clark, Ravi Kane Receive Awards from AIChE’s Society for Biological Engineering |url=https://www.aiche.org/about/press/releases/10-13-2014/douglas-clark-ravi-kane-receive-awards-aiches-society-biological-engineering |access-date=9 October 2023 |publisher=American Institute of Chemical Engineers |date=13 October 2014}}</ref> Clark is a 2019 member of the [[United States National Academy of Engineering]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Professor Douglas S. Clark |url=https://www.nae.edu/204084/Professor-Douglas-S-Clark |access-date=9 October 2023 |publisher=United States National Academy of Engineering}}</ref>
